messages:
amira: @channel Quick heads-up: SDK v4.1.0 will ship next week and includes two coordinated changes that affect integrations and docs: 1) telemetry switches from auto-collection to explicit opt-in (privacy-first), and 2) the legacy ~/.redwood/runtime-flags.json file is removed in favor of per-process --runtime-config v2 flags. Full migration guide published: https://go.redwood/docs/sdk-v4-1-migration :loudspeaker:
noah: Can you summarize customer impact? Will anything break for our hosted API users?
jen: TL;DR: most apps will be fine. Breaking surface is only if you relied on the old runtime-flags file (we'll auto-fallback for 30 days) or relied on implicit telemetry being present for internal monitoring. Hosted API pub/sub telemetry continues server-side; SDK telemetry (client-side usage / env metadata) will stop unless explicitly opted in.
amira: Timeline: GA in 7 days. We’ll start a 30d migration window where v4.1 warns to stderr (but still accepts legacy flags). After 30d, SDK v4.1+ will stop reading the legacy file. Telemetry: immediate opt-out by default on GA; we will not send client telemetry unless opt-in env var or config is set.
jen: Migration snippets — Node (new opt-in):
```js
// explicitly opt in to client telemetry
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({telemetry: {enabled: true}});
```
Python (env var):
```bash
export REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY_OPT_IN=true
python app.py
```
legacy runtime flags example (DEPRECATED):
```json
// ~/.redwood/runtime-flags.json  <-- ignored after grace period
{"enable_fast_kv": true, "quant_mode": "int8"}
```
noah: What about Dedicated / Private customers who use config management to drop the flags file?
ops: Ops note: Dedicated clusters with config-management that wrote the flags file to home will need to switch to the new --runtime-config JSON mount or set the REDWOOD_RUNTIME_CONFIG_PATH env var. We added an automated transformer in the management console to convert common keys.
docs-bot: Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4212 — includes migration checklist, sample helm manifests, and a troubleshooting faq. Please review the snippets section for accurate copy.
luis: We need a customer comms plan. Can we get an exec-friendly blurb and an FAQ for sales & CSMs?
amira: Yes — comms schedule: day 0 (announce in #customers and release notes), day 2 (email to active customers with Dedicated/Private footprints), day 7 (GA release + banner on Console), day 14 (reminder + migration telemetry report for opted-in customers). I'll post the CSM FAQ by EOD.
jen: Quick note for SDK maintainers: run the compatibility-checker against our top-100 repos (job queued) and add a --telemetry-deprecation warning to the legacy loader.
dev-bot: Release artifact pushed: @release-bot tag v4.1.0-rc2 (sha: a1b2c3d). Integration tests: started.
noah: Thanks — who owns making the telemetry setting prominent in quickstarts?
amira: DevEx (jen + noah) — please update the quickstarts, the interactive playground, and the SDK init templates. I'll follow up in #devex with files to change.
ops: FYI — Private packages customers: if you have HSM/KMS-based telemetry keys configured, those are unaffected; this change only affects automatic client-side payloads.
luis: Adding a comms ask: include a short migration snippet for mobile SDKs (we have a few customers on iOS/Android still using the flags file).
jen: Will add mobile snippets to PR.
amira: Thanks everyone. If you see anything critical in the migration PRs, tag me. :thumbsup:
